global.headline: TRUMP CALLS OFF PLANNED IRAN STRIKES, CITES 'OUTLINES' OF A HORMUZ-AND-NUCLEAR DEAL, AS GAZA TOLL HITS A WEEKS-HIGH AND ISRAEL KILLS HEZBOLLAH FIGHTERS IN LEBANON
summary: President Trump said Saturday he had cancelled a planned joint US-Israel attack on Iranian energy infrastructure — reportedly imminent, according to earlier US media reports — after Middle Eastern allies led by Saudi Arabia, fearing a wider war, asked him to pursue a deal instead. On Truth Social, Trump said the US had been asked "to hold off any attack in that the perimeters of a deal has been agreed to," adding: "Based on this request, I have agreed... to cancel the attack, subject to being able to rapidly make a DEAL." He said the outline includes the "Immediate, Complete, and Total OPENING OF THE HORMUZ STRAIT, and an end to Iran's nuclear threat," with Israel committed alongside him. The reversal appeared to catch Israel off guard and undercut Netanyahu's claim days earlier that he and Trump were in lockstep on Iran; Trump said Sunday that US-Iran negotiations will resume Monday.

Iran's response was guarded rather than celebratory: Foreign Minister Araghchi held calls with counterparts in Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey warning that any renewed US or Israeli strike would be met with a "proportionate response," while President Pezeshkian said Tehran "must strive to compel the enemy to honor what it signed" under the original memorandum of understanding. Araghchi separately said Iran-Oman talks on Hormuz's reopening are in their "final stage." No ceasefire document or signed agreement exists yet — only a mutual pause and a stated outline.

The pause did not extend to Gaza or Lebanon. Israeli strikes killed at least 18 Palestinians across Gaza City, Deir al-Balah and Khan Younis on Sunday — the highest single-day toll in weeks — with Israel's military saying one strike on a Deir al-Balah apartment targeted two Hamas "Nukhba" force commanders; Energy Minister Eli Cohen said there is "no deal to halt attacks" and that Israel, which already controls 70% of the Strip, should take full control. In Lebanon, the Israeli military said its troops killed several Hezbollah members overnight in a ground encounter on the Ali al-Taher Ridge, about six miles north of the border, wounding one IDF officer — a rare direct clash rather than a strike, which Netanyahu framed as a response to what he called Hezbollah's "blatant violation" of the ceasefire days earlier.
global.geopolitical: A cancelled joint US-Israel strike, credited publicly to Saudi lobbying, is the most consequential de-escalation signal of the war since it reignited in early July — but it rests on an unsigned "outline" rather than a ceasefire, has visibly strained Washington's coordination with Netanyahu, and runs in parallel with Gaza's worst single-day death toll in weeks and Israel's first reported ground clash with Hezbollah in months, underscoring that any Iran-specific pause leaves the wider regional conflict largely untouched.
global.socioeconomic: Brent crude fell as much as 7.3% to $81.55 a barrel and WTI slid near $80 on the news, unwinding much of July's ~25% run-up in a single session; the drop is the market's clearest vote yet that traders see the Iran track specifically, not the broader Gaza-Lebanon violence, as the dominant driver of the war-risk premium priced into oil.

global.headline: SUICIDE BOMBER KILLS AT LEAST 14 AT ANTI-MILITANT RALLY IN PAKISTAN'S SWAT VALLEY
summary: A suicide bomber struck a rally of residents demonstrating against militancy in Kabal, a town in Swat Valley, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, on Sunday, killing at least 14 people — including five police officers — and wounding more than two dozen others. Demonstrators had gathered near a local police station chanting anti-militant slogans and demanding the state do more to guarantee security, accusing authorities of failing to act decisively against resurgent militant groups after years of violence that devastated the region.
global.geopolitical: Striking a rally explicitly organised against militancy shows Pakistan's resurgent insurgency is willing to attack the very civilians pushing back against it, undercutting Islamabad's counter-insurgency narrative in a province it has repeatedly declared largely pacified.
global.socioeconomic: Swat Valley's tourism-dependent economy, still recovering from a prior decade of militancy, faces a fresh setback as renewed high-casualty violence reinforces the security perceptions that have kept visitor numbers and outside investment below pre-insurgency levels.

global.headline: AT LEAST FIVE DEAD, 41 MISSING AS FIRE ENGULFS INDONESIAN FERRY OFF JAVA
summary: The ferry Mutiara Sentosa 2, carrying 271 people — 232 passengers and 39 crew — from Surabaya to Makassar, caught fire in waters off Sumenep regency, East Java, around 6-7am Sunday. Nearby vessels rescued 225 people and recovered five bodies; 41 remained unaccounted for by Sunday afternoon. The Indonesian Navy deployed a warship and rescue vessels from Surabaya to the scene, though rough seas forced one rigid inflatable boat to turn back. The cause of the fire was not immediately known and remains under investigation.
global.geopolitical: Indonesia's chronic run of fatal ferry incidents — this is the latest in a series stretching back years — keeps domestic maritime-safety regulation under international scrutiny even as the archipelago's inter-island shipping remains largely outside the safety frameworks built for commercial cargo and container traffic.
global.socioeconomic: Ferries remain the primary transport link for millions of Indonesians across the archipelago; repeated fatal incidents like this one expose how far search-and-rescue capacity and fleet safety investment continue to lag the volume of people who depend on ageing domestic vessels.

global.headline: UKRAINE STRIKES DEEP INTO RUSSIA, HITTING A STRATEGIC BOMBER BASE AND A MAJOR OIL REFINERY
summary: Ukraine's armed forces struck the Saratov oil refinery — one of the Volga region's largest, with roughly 7 million tonnes/year of capacity — the nearby Engels airfield, home to Tu-95MS and Tu-160 strategic bombers, an oil depot in Russia's Kaluga region, and an attack-drone launch site in Bryansk region overnight into Monday. Ukraine's General Staff and President Zelensky confirmed the strikes, reporting direct hits and fires at both the refinery and the airfield; the regional governor confirmed the area had come under attack and said preliminary reports indicated casualties, without giving a figure.
global.geopolitical: Hitting one of Russia's two principal strategic-bomber bases directly, rather than only refineries and drone infrastructure, signals Kyiv's long-range strike campaign is now willing to target the core of Russia's nuclear-capable long-range aviation fleet, not just its war economy.
global.socioeconomic: Ukraine's sustained refinery-strike campaign continues to squeeze Russian domestic fuel supply even as Moscow runs its own parallel campaign against Ukrainian filling stations, a mutually reinforcing energy-infrastructure war whose fuel-access and price costs increasingly fall on civilians on both sides.

global.headline: EU CONFIRMS TUESDAY EMERGENCY MEETING ON CEUTA AS SPAIN CALLS ITALY AND DENMARK'S RESPONSE 'SELFISH'
summary: Ireland, which holds the rotating EU Council presidency, confirmed it will convene Tuesday's Justice and Home Affairs Council — chaired by Irish Justice Minister Jim O'Callaghan — to address the Ceuta crisis, after 22 member states, in a letter initiated by Italy and Denmark, demanded emergency talks. Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez wrote to European Commission President von der Leyen calling Italy and Denmark's push "selfish, polarising and unlawful" and separately requested a full 27-nation interior-ministers meeting. On the ground, Spain says the crossing has "almost entirely reversed" with most of the roughly 60,000 arrivals already returned to Morocco, but far-right leaders are now calling on Madrid to expel remaining migrants, while exhausted holdouts shelter in makeshift conditions on Ceuta's streets and beaches.
global.geopolitical: Spain's public rebuke of two fellow EU states, rather than a unified bloc response, shows how sharply national politics — not just migration numbers — now divides Europe's response to a single-territory crisis, handing the continent's far right an opening to set the terms of the debate even in a country where it has traditionally had less purchase.
global.socioeconomic: The prolonged limbo facing exhausted holdouts even as Spain declares the crossing largely over shows a returns-and-processing system built for routine flows remains overwhelmed by a shock of this scale, with humanitarian and local-services costs still accruing daily.

singapore.headline: EIGHT MEN, ONE WOMAN CHARGED OVER SEXUAL EXPLOITATION OF TWO MINORS IN SINGAPORE
summary: A 20-year-old woman and eight men aged 20 to 41 were due in court Monday after police said a preliminary probe found the woman recruited and exploited two victims, both under 18 at the time, by facilitating commercial sexual services for profit and knowingly receiving payments linked to a trafficked victim; she also faces cheating charges. Follow-up investigations identified the eight men as having separately obtained commercial sexual services from one of the victims.
singapore.geopolitical: The case adds to a steady run of child sexual-exploitation prosecutions Singapore has brought over the past year, part of a broader regional pattern of online-enabled recruitment of minors that law-enforcement agencies across Southeast Asia have flagged as a growing cross-border threat.
singapore.socioeconomic: Prosecuting a network of buyers alongside a single alleged recruiter will test how Singapore's courts weigh culpability across an exploitation ring, a distinction likely to shape sentencing norms and deterrence messaging for similar cases.

singapore.headline: FAULTY DRY RISING MAIN FORCED CLEMENTI FIRE CREWS TO HAUL HOSES UP EIGHT FLOORS, SCDF SAYS
summary: SCDF confirmed the dry rising main serving Block 309 Clementi Avenue 4 was not in proper working condition during last Thursday's fatal fire, forcing firefighters to haul hoses up eight floors by hand instead of drawing water directly at the fire floor — a delay in an incident that killed one resident and injured two firefighters. The finding extends the investigation opened after the blaze, which also saw about 40 residents evacuated.
singapore.geopolitical: The equipment failure raises fresh questions about routine maintenance inspection regimes for essential fire-safety systems in older HDB blocks, echoing a 2019 SCDF warning to a different town council over non-functioning firefighting equipment.
singapore.socioeconomic: Restoring confidence in dry riser and hose-reel maintenance across ageing housing stock will likely mean added inspection costs passed through town-council conservancy charges, a small but real addition to the upkeep costs already associated with older estates.

singapore.headline: WORKERS' PARTY TO TABLE PARLIAMENT MOTION SETTING OUT ITS OWN VISION FOR SINGAPORE'S ECONOMY
summary: The Workers' Party will table a motion in Parliament on 4 August setting out its own vision for Singapore's economy and responding to the Government's economic plans, with most of its 12 MPs expected to speak on themes including innovation, the cost of doing business, jobs and helping local businesses regionalise. Aljunied GRC MP Kenneth Tiong filed the motion, seconded by Sengkang GRC MP Jamus Lim; its first part asks whether the House believes in a more equal and inclusive economy with room for entrepreneurs to experiment.
singapore.geopolitical: The motion is WP's most substantive attempt yet to present a comprehensive economic alternative to the PAP government's roadmap, ahead of a debate expected to feature prominently as both sides sharpen their platforms.
singapore.socioeconomic: A substantive parliamentary debate could pressure the government to respond directly to opposition proposals on business costs and regionalisation support, sharpening the domestic contest over how to help SMEs navigate an increasingly tariff-fragmented global trading environment — a live concern given the 12.5% US forced-labour tariff Singapore is already contesting.

word.definition: A state of temporary disuse, suspension or inactivity, typically pending some future resolution — most often used in the phrase "in abeyance."
word.etymology: From Anglo-Norman French abeance ("gaping, longing, expectation"), from Old French abeer ("to gape at, aspire to"), from Latin ad- ("to") + batare ("to gape"); originally a legal term for a property title or right temporarily unclaimed while awaiting a determination of its rightful holder.
word.example: Trump's planned joint strikes on Iran's energy infrastructure were placed in abeyance Saturday — suspended, not cancelled outright — contingent on Tehran "rapidly" delivering the Hormuz reopening and nuclear rollback he says the two sides have already outlined.
